PASS. The diff implements PMAT-065 (#65) cleanly and satisfies all acceptance criteria in `docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml` without touching out-of-scope workflows or rulesets:

1. **Fan-in `gate` job**: `.github/workflows/gate.yml` defines `gate` (`if: always()`, `needs: [book-build]`) triggered on `pull_request`, `push` to `main`, `merge_group`, and `workflow_dispatch`. It rejects an empty `needs` map (`total -eq 0`) and rejects any needed job whose result is not `"success"` (failing on `failure`, `cancelled`, or `skipped`).
2. **`book-build` parity & anti-vacuity**: `book-build` installs `mdBook v0.4.40` (matching `.github/workflows/pages.yml`), runs `mdbook build` (with `create-missing = false` in `book.toml`), and verifies both `test -s book/index.html` and `[ "$pages" -gt 1 ]`.
3. **Planted controls verified**: Inspected commits `9c6cf4b556` (`planted/PMAT-065-green`), `c2c5b9ecd7` (`planted/PMAT-065-red`), and `e651e9ebcc` (`planted/PMAT-065-vacuous`); their diffs match the receipt claims.
4. **Answer to scope question**: Yes, gating on `book-build` alone is right. `test.yml` (#53, #56 — uses deprecated `actions/upload-artifact@v3`), `pmat-dogfood.yml` (also uses `@v3` actions and fails link checks), `mdbook test`, and the link check (#58) have never passed on `main`. Wiring broken checks into the required `gate` check now would keep the merge queue deadlocked and block the PRs that fix those checks from merging. Requiring three green nights on `main` and explicit owner approval before adding a check to `gate.needs` is the sound Jidoka policy.
